right-rule.prompt:
Educational right-of-way diagram for a Danish driving-theory app, seen straight from above (bird's-eye view), right-hand traffic as in Denmark.
THE SCENE: a simple square four-way crossroads of two straight two-way roads, one lane in each direction, in the middle of the picture. Medium grey asphalt, a white broken centre line on each road that stops at the edge of the junction, light grey pavements with thin kerbs, small green verges at the four corners. NO traffic signs, NO traffic lights, NO stop lines, NO give-way triangles (shark teeth), NO zebra crossings: an unmarked junction.
ROAD USERS (colour code used strictly):
- RED car (must give way): in the right-hand lane of the bottom road, driving up towards the junction, stopped just before the edge of the junction. A short DASHED ORANGE arrow from its nose ends before the junction.
- BLUE car (has right of way): in the right-hand lane of the right road (the upper lane of that road), driving towards the left, so it comes from the RED car's right. A SOLID GREEN arrow runs from its nose straight across the junction to the left side.
- No other road users.
MUST NOT APPEAR: signs, lights, stop lines, shark teeth, extra vehicles, people, text, letters, numbers, logos, watermarks, left-hand traffic.
Style: a clean flat vector illustration for a Danish driving-theory app, NOT photorealistic and NOT a 3D render: simple clean shapes, flat even colours, crisp edges, only very soft shadows, uncluttered, plenty of space around the junction; simple rounded cars seen from above. No text anywhere.

exit-property.prompt:
Educational right-of-way diagram for a Danish driving-theory app, seen straight from above (bird's-eye view), right-hand traffic as in Denmark.
THE SCENE: across the middle of the picture runs one straight two-way road from left to right, medium grey asphalt with a white broken centre line. Along the BOTTOM side of the road, from the road outwards: a cycle track (a slightly raised strip of asphalt, separated from the road by a low kerb), then a light grey paved pavement, then a small parking area of a shop with a few marked white parking bays. A driveway (a lowered kerb) connects the parking area across the pavement and the cycle track to the road.
ROAD USERS (colour code used strictly):
- RED car (must give way): leaving the parking area through the driveway, facing up towards the road, stopped on the parking area just before the pavement. A short DASHED ORANGE arrow from its nose ends before the pavement.
- A PEDESTRIAN in a yellow jacket walking along the pavement, just about to pass in front of the red car, with a small SOLID GREEN arrow showing the path along the pavement.
- A CYCLIST in a purple jacket riding along the cycle track towards the driveway, with a SOLID GREEN arrow along the cycle track.
- A BLUE car driving along the road in its right-hand lane (the lane nearer the bottom), approaching from the left, with a SOLID GREEN arrow along the road.
MUST NOT APPEAR: traffic signs, traffic lights, shark teeth, extra vehicles or people, text, letters, numbers, logos, watermarks, shop names, left-hand traffic.
Style: a clean flat vector illustration for a Danish driving-theory app, NOT photorealistic and NOT a 3D render: simple clean shapes, flat even colours, crisp edges, only very soft shadows, uncluttered, plenty of space; simple rounded cars and people seen from above. No text anywhere.
